questions.question: Which versions of Python and scikit-learn were used when the model was trained?
questions.answer: Python 3.10 and scikit-learn v1.2 were used [page 4].

questions.question: On what platform was the model developed and trained?
questions.answer: The model was developed and trained using Google Colab [page 4].

questions.question: How many rows and columns did the raw data contain before cleaning?
questions.answer: The raw data contained approximately 7,000 rows and 68 columns [page 3].

questions.question: How much of the model's feature importance is attributed to the toilet-related feature?
questions.answer: The Toilet Score has an importance score of 0.198 [page 5].

questions.question: How fast was the inference service on average over the repeated test requests?
questions.answer: The average latency measured across 100 sequential inference requests was 173 ms under test deployment conditions [page 6].

questions.question: Which techniques do the authors plan to use later to explain the model's predictions?
questions.answer: The authors plan to integrate Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques, specifically SHAP and LIME [page 7].

questions.question: By how much did the automated registrar system in prior work cut data entry time?
questions.answer: The automated school registrar system resulted in a 40% reduction in data entry time [page 2].

questions.question: What does the name of the system mean in English?
questions.answer: The term “E-Manyata Pranali” translates loosely from Marathi to “Digital Recognition System” [page 1].

questions.question: How many Moderate-quality schools did the model classify correctly on the test set?
questions.answer: The model correctly classified 560 Moderate-quality schools on the test set [page 5].

questions.question: How many test samples belong to the Moderate class?
questions.answer: There are 602 test samples in the Moderate class [page 5].

questions.question: How do the weighted F1-scores on the training data and the test data compare?
questions.answer: The weighted F1-scores are closely aligned, with 0.97 on the training data compared to 0.94 on the test data [page 5].

questions.question: Which existing system only partly supports a real-time admin dashboard?
questions.answer: The Digital Approval System [7] only partly supports a real-time admin dashboard [page 7].

questions.question: Which two of the existing systems offer only partial UDISE authentication?
How is the safety score calculated from the raw facility columns?
questions.answer:
The safety score is calculated using the formula [page 3]:

$$\text{SAFETY\_SCORE} = \frac{\text{avail\_ramps} + \text{avail\_handrails} + \text{med\_chk}}{3}$$

It sums the columns for ramp availability (`avail_ramps`), handrail availability (`avail_handrails`), and medical checkups (`med_chk`), divided by 3 [page 3].

What was the average response time of the prediction endpoint, and what upper limit was it designed to stay under?
questions.answer: The average response time of the inference endpoint was 173 ms across 100 sequential requests under test conditions [page 6]. It was designed to stay under an upper limit of 200 ms (<200 ms latency) [page 2, page 6].
